files.role: Public generic exponentially growing linked blocks, borrowed/owned iterators, equality and memory-estimation implementations; private block state and local tests.
ranges: SPDX metadata and imports bind the implementation to std::collections::LinkedList and the local DeepSizeOf trait. No allocator or concurrency abstraction is introduced.

ExpLinkedList<T> derives Debug, Clone and Default and privately stores LinkedList<Vec<T>>, an explicit element count, and a u16 capacity limit. Documentation describes exponentially larger blocks to reduce allocation frequency. Limit zero means unlimited; its u16 representation is explicitly intended to keep the limit compact. This is a limit on newly chosen block capacities, not a total-element bound.

`new` starts with no blocks, len=0, limit=0. `with_capacity(capacity)` always pushes one Vec::with_capacity(capacity), even for zero, and starts len=0, limit=0. Consequently preallocated empty and newly constructed empty have different block-presence states; no elements are initialized by reserving.

The consuming builder `with_capacity_limit(mut self, limit:u16)->Self` only replaces limit and returns self. It does not shrink existing blocks or reject zero/large existing capacity. Its documented purpose is avoiding large allocations at high element counts.

push checks the last Vec: if full, it doubles capacity unless a positive limit is reached or exceeded, then appends a Vec with the capped capacity; with no last Vec it appends capacity one. do_push unwraps the now-present last block, pushes the value, then increments len. Doubling and len increment have no overflow guard. A pre-existing zero-capacity block computes another zero capacity and delegates actual growth to Vec::push; the configured limit is not validated against this dependency-selected growth. Setting a smaller limit cannot change an existing larger block.

pop examines the last block; an empty block is removed and pop recursively retries. A nonempty block decrements len and pops one value; no block means None. Removing a last value does not immediately remove its now-empty block. Ordering is LIFO across blocks and within each Vec. Repeated empty blocks cost recursive retries.

clear drops all LinkedList blocks and resets len, preserving limit. len returns the stored count. is_empty calls inner.is_empty rather than len==0: with_capacity creates a zero-length list for which is_empty is false, and popping the last element leaves the same discrepancy until an extra pop or clear removes the block.

size returns (len + spare capacity in the last Vec)*size_of::<T>() + size_of::<Self>() + number_of_blocks*size_of::<Vec<T>>(). The comments describe allocated element capacity and warn that nested heap contents such as String data are absent. The formula counts the complete inline T representation, not a String allocation. It omits LinkedList link-node overhead and allocator overhead; it is an estimate, not exact total retained memory. The formula assumes earlier blocks contribute their live length, not all earlier spare capacity.

iter returns ExpLinkedListIter::new(self). block_iter maps LinkedList iteration to each Vec slice, preserving block and element insertion order and exposing empty blocks as empty slices. Neither creates copies of T.

The DeepSizeOf implementation sums each Vec::deep_size_of_children using one mutable context. It includes Vec allocated element capacity and descendant heap estimates, but no explicit Vec-header or LinkedList-node accounting. The default trait method separately adds size_of_val(self). See the Vec rule and trait default in rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:38-44 and rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:166-174.

FromIterator takes the iterator lower size_hint bound as first block capacity when positive, otherwise one, then pushes each item. It always allocates a block through with_capacity, so even collecting an empty iterator yields len=0 but is_empty=false. The default growth limit remains zero. A misleading upstream lower bound can affect allocation size; no extra cap is applied.

PartialEq requires T:PartialEq, zips both borrowed iterators, and returns all element comparisons true. It never compares lengths: equal prefixes of different lengths compare equal, and any empty list compares equal to any other list. Eq is nevertheless implemented for T:Eq. Static consequence: [1,2]==[1] and [1]==[1,3], while [1,2]!=[1,3], violating equivalence transitivity. This is current code behavior, not the expected list-equality contract or an executed regression.

Public ExpLinkedListIter stores private linked-block iterator, optional current slice iterator and the initial total len. Its public new constructor borrows the list, starts without a current block and copies the element count. The borrow enforces source lifetime and forbids ordinary concurrent mutation through that shared reference.

Iterator Item is &'a T. next first tries the current slice, then installs the next block iterator and recursively retries, skipping exhausted/empty blocks; no more blocks returns None. It never decrements the saved len. size_hint always returns (original_len,Some(original_len)), including after yields and exhaustion, so its positive lower bound becomes inaccurate. No ExactSizeIterator implementation is declared here.

Public ExpLinkedListIntoIter privately owns linked-list IntoIter<Vec<T>>, an optional Vec IntoIter<T>, and the copied original len. Its public new consumes ExpLinkedList and moves the blocks into the iterator; it does not clone items.

The owned Iterator yields T. It follows the same current-block/next-block recursive progression as the borrowed version and also never updates len. Its size_hint therefore reports the original element count after consumption. Exhausted blocks are advanced past as owned iterators are replaced.

IntoIterator for ExpLinkedList<T> declares Item=T and IntoIter=ExpLinkedListIntoIter<T>; into_iter consumes self and delegates to the owned constructor. Borrowed traversal is provided by iter; no IntoIterator for &ExpLinkedList is declared in this file.

The cfg(test) module imports the list and defines shared helper test_exp_linked_list: require 100 elements/nonempty, pop 50 items from 99 down to 50, verify len=50 and forward iteration over 0..50, clear, then assert len=0/is_empty and pop=None. The helper is not itself marked test.

test_exp_linked_list_basic creates new, pushes 0..100 while checking length after every push, then invokes the shared helper. It exercises default block growth indirectly, not exact per-block capacities.
test_exp_linked_list_from collects 0..100 through FromIterator and invokes the helper, covering nonempty preallocation and retained element order.

test_exp_linked_list_with_capacity_limit sets ten, pushes 100 values with count checks, asserts the last Vec capacity equals ten, then invokes the helper. It does not test existing oversized/zero-capacity blocks, equality with unequal lengths, size_hint after advancement, or len=0 with retained blocks. All tests were read, not executed.

files.role: Public deep-memory-estimation trait and pointer-deduplication context, derive-macro re-export, standard-library/Arrow implementations, private recursive Arrow-buffer accounting, and local tests.
ranges: SPDX lines, public re-export of lance_derive::DeepSizeOf in the macro namespace, and imports for size_of/size_of_val, collections, atomics, Arc/locks, Arrow arrays/buffers/data. The same DeepSizeOf spelling is also used for the trait below; derive expansion implementation is in another crate and remains pending.

Context is a public struct with a private HashSet<usize> of seen identities. Default calls new; new starts empty. mark_seen(ptr) directly returns set insertion success, true only for a newly inserted integer. The caller supplies pointer identity and a mutable context; there is no reset API or synchronization layer. The context tracking set itself is not charged by these formulas.

DeepSizeOf is public. Its default deep_size_of adds size_of_val(self) to deep_size_of_children with a fresh Context; the latter is required and receives mutable traversal state. Separate top-level calls cannot deduplicate against each other. Implementations must count descendant heap storage without recounting their own inline footprint and should propagate the same context when deduplication is intended.

Private impl_deep_size_primitive macro emits trait implementations returning zero children. The invocation covers u8/u16/u32/u64/u128/usize, i8/i16/i32/i64/i128/isize, f32/f64, bool and (). This list excludes char and other numeric wrappers; their support is not implied by the macro. Their inline size still comes from the default method.

str reports zero child storage because its dynamically sized bytes are its own size_of_val; String reports capacity, not current length, as heap children. Thus direct str and owned String accounting use different ownership boundaries.

bytes::Bytes uses as_ptr as a usize key. On first sight it charges self.len(), otherwise zero. This is exact start-pointer deduplication, not underlying-allocation identity or capacity accounting: distinct offsets can be counted separately and equal-start views of different lengths are sensitive to visitation order. These limitations follow from the key/formula; external Bytes allocation details are not reviewed here.

AtomicU64 and AtomicUsize both return zero children without loading their stored numeric value. The top-level default counts their inline representation. No other atomic type implementation is present in this range.

Fixed [T;N] and dynamically sized [T] sum only element child sizes using the same context; inline elements are already counted by the owner or size_of_val. Slice comments explicitly identify Box<[T]> and Arc<[T]> as owners that count slice bytes; adding those bytes again in the slice implementation would double-count them.

RwLock<T> obtains a read guard and Mutex<T> an exclusive guard, then delegates to protected T children. A poisoned-lock Err returns zero, silently undercounting children. These are blocking lock acquisitions with no timeout and no Result returned; memory estimation can wait on contention or deadlock under an incompatible already-held lock. The lock wrapper inline footprint comes from its owner/default method.

Private impl_deep_size_tuple macro emits generic implementations requiring every tuple component DeepSizeOf, destructures self under allow(non_snake_case), and sums each component children. Invocations cover tuple arities two through six only. The tuple inline layout/padding is counted by its owning object/default method, not by this sum.

Vec<T> charges capacity*size_of::<T>() plus children of live elements only. Uninitialized spare capacity contributes bytes but is not traversed. The Vec header is counted at the enclosing inline boundary. Arithmetic is ordinary usize multiplication/addition, with no overflow handling.

Box<T:?Sized> always charges pointee size_of_val plus pointee children. Arc<T:?Sized> first casts its data pointer through *const () to usize (discarding metadata), deduplicates it, and only on first sight charges pointee size plus children. Arc control-block/refcount and allocator overhead are not explicitly counted. Marking before recursive descent permits repeated Arc identities to be skipped; this is not general graph-cycle detection for arbitrary custom implementations.
Option<T> delegates to Some inner children or returns zero for None. The discriminant and inline T storage are left to the parent/default footprint rather than counted again.

HashMap<K,V,S> supports any hasher type parameter and estimates backing storage as capacity*(size_of::<K>()+size_of::<V>()+1), then adds live key/value children. The comment calls the one-byte term approximate control metadata and notes capacity/buckets; the code uses reported capacity directly. Alignment, allocator overhead and exact table layout are not measured, so this is an estimate.

HashSet<K> (default hasher form) estimates capacity*(size_of::<K>()+1) plus live key children. It does not define the generic-S HashSet implementation analogous to HashMap. The one-byte overhead is approximate.

BTreeMap estimates len*(size_of::<K>()+size_of::<V>()+3*size_of::<usize>()) plus live key/value children. BTreeSet uses len*(size_of::<K>()+3*size_of::<usize>()) plus live key children. Comments motivate roughly three pointer words per entry based on an average B-tree node. These formulas do not inspect actual node count, node occupancy or allocations.

Private record_array_data walks every data buffer, adding its capacity if its as_ptr integer is first seen; it similarly accounts for the null bit-buffer obtained through inner().inner(), then recursively visits child_data. The shared Context deduplicates identical start addresses across descendants. No explicit ArrayData metadata or child-vector allocation charge is added.

The dyn Array implementation calls to_data and delegates to record_array_data. The comment describes to_data as cloning Arcs rather than data bytes and says this creates a small O(number of buffers) metadata cost; that is the source comment, not an independently verified property of every dependency Array implementation. The returned estimate accounts for the traversed buffers.

RecordBatch sums deep_size_of_children for each column Arc with one context. It has no explicit charge here for its column-vector allocation or schema metadata. Default deep_size_of separately counts the inline RecordBatch. Sharing the same Array Arc across columns is deduplicated by Arc accounting before buffer traversal.

ScalarBuffer<T> is implemented where T:ArrowNativeType. It obtains the inner Buffer, deduplicates as_ptr, and charges capacity only once. The comment chooses capacity rather than slice length because sliced buffers retain backing storage; the implementation key is still a start pointer, not an owning-allocation identifier. Changed start pointers can therefore defeat same-key deduplication.

The cfg(test) module imports Arrow fixtures and the local trait/context. test_basic_record_batch makes one Int32 column [1,2,3] and asserts deep size >=12 bytes. It verifies a lower bound, not exact RecordBatch metadata accounting.

test_same_batch_dedup uses one Context for repeated RecordBatch child-size calls; first must be positive, second exactly zero. The test deliberately avoids fresh-context deep_size_of, demonstrating traversal-local deduplication.
test_arc_dedup clones an Arc<RecordBatch>, then measures both with the same Context and requires first positive, second zero. This exercises shared batch identity before child traversal.

test_multi_column_shared_array places two clones of the same Int32 Array Arc in a two-column batch and compares its child estimate with a one-column batch measured using a separate Context. Equality proves the tested shared-array case is counted once; it does not prove equality of complete allocated batch sizes.

test_nested_struct_array constructs Int32 and String children under one StructArray in a RecordBatch. It requires deep size >12, a weak traversal lower bound rather than an exact byte total or proof of every child-buffer contribution.

test_std_types checks exact inline u32 size, String >=header+5, Vec<u32> >=header+three element bytes, and Arc<u32> children four then zero in one Context. Lower-bound assertions permit extra capacity/overhead; the Arc test isolates identity deduplication.

test_derive_macro imports the derive macro, defines local Outer {count:u64,label:String,inner:Inner} and Inner {values:Vec<u32>} with derives, then requires size >=size_of::<Outer>()+5+12 for the constructed fixture. It tests macro usability/recursive heap accounting at a lower bound, not the macro implementation itself. No local cases validate Bytes aliases, scalar-buffer offset aliases, poisoned locks or collection-estimate accuracy. Tests were read, not executed.

files.role: Public extension trait for joining object-store Path components, without filesystem IO.
ranges: SPDX metadata and object_store::path::Path import; Path here is not std::path::Path.
LancePathExt is public and requires `child_path(&self,path:&Path)->Path`. It returns an owned path directly rather than Result.

The Path implementation clones self into a working full_path, then for each supplied path.parts() replaces it with full_path.clone().child(part), returning the final value. With zero parts this is the base clone. It delegates parsing/component and child-joining semantics to object_store and performs no IO. files.role: Public stream/span adapter and exact tracing target/event-name constants, with no local event emitter or tests.
ranges: SPDX metadata and futures::Stream, pin_project::pin_project and tracing::Span imports establish dependencies for stream projection and scoped span entry.

InstrumentedStream<I:Stream> is public, with private #[pin] stream and unpinned Span; #[pin_project] supplies safe field projections. Callers normally construct it through the extension trait because fields are private.

The Stream implementation has Item=I::Item. poll_next projects the pinned wrapper, enters the stored span with a local guard, and delegates one poll to the inner stream. The guard ends on return, including Pending; it does not keep a span entered across the whole asynchronous wait. No custom size_hint or Drop behavior is implemented.

StreamTracingExt is a public trait without a supertrait; its two consuming methods each require Self:Stream+Sized. stream_in_current_span chooses context implicitly; stream_in_span accepts an explicit Span. The comment gives the naming reason as avoiding ambiguity with a similarly named instrumentation trait; no dependency trait implementation is changed.

The blanket implementation applies to every S:Stream. stream_in_current_span captures Span::current at wrapper construction and forwards to stream_in_span; the explicit form stores self and the supplied span. Construction does not poll the stream or enter the span.

File audit constants: TRACE_FILE_AUDIT="lance::file_audit"; AUDIT_MODE_CREATE="create", DELETE="delete", DELETE_UNVERIFIED="delete_unverified"; AUDIT_TYPE_DELETION="deletion", MANIFEST="manifest", INDEX="index", DATA="data", TRANSACTION="transaction"; TRACE_FILE_CREATE="create". All are public &str values; sharing the string "create" does not mean sharing one semantic field.

IO constants: TRACE_IO_EVENTS="lance::io_events"; IO_TYPE_OPEN_SCALAR="open_scalar_index", VECTOR="open_vector_index", FRAG_REUSE="open_frag_reuse_index", MEM_WAL="open_mem_wal_index"; IO_TYPE_LOAD_VECTOR_PART="load_vector_part", SCALAR_PART="load_scalar_part". files.role: Public power-of-two, alignment-padding and bit-width helpers, a private lookup table, doctests and local numerical tests.
ranges: SPDX metadata and documentation introduce is_pwr_two(u64)->bool. It computes n&(n-1)==0. Doctest positives are one, two and 1024; negatives are three and 1000. Zero is not guarded: subtracting one underflows with checked arithmetic; when subtraction wraps, zero returns true. It is therefore not a total mathematical nonzero-power-of-two predicate.

pad_bytes<const ALIGN:usize>(n:usize)->usize debug-asserts is_pwr_two(ALIGN as u64), then computes (ALIGN-(n&(ALIGN-1)))&(ALIGN-1). For a valid nonzero power-of-two alignment it gives zero for aligned n, otherwise bytes to next boundary, without first adding ALIGN to n. Doctest ALIGN=8 checks n=0/1/8/9 gives 0/7/0/7. Invalid alignment is not validated with a returned error and debug_assert may be disabled.

pad_bytes_to(n:usize,align:usize)->usize implements the same mask formula and debug assertion with runtime alignment. Examples use alignment eight and the same four cases. Non-power-of-two inputs need not give modular padding, and zero can cause arithmetic underflow; no release-mode input validation is added.

pad_bytes_u64<const ALIGN:u64>(n:u64)->u64 is the u64 version of the same mask formula and debug check; its examples mirror the usize functions. Correctness requires a nonzero power-of-two ALIGN. Arithmetic/checking behavior for invalid inputs follows the same unguarded subtractions.

LOG_TABLE_256 is private [u8;256]. Despite the logarithm comment, entries encode bit width: 0->0, 1->1, 2..3->2, 4..7->3, doubling groups up to 128..255->8. It is a byte lookup for the routine below; there is no runtime table generation.

log_2_ceil(val:u32)->u32 always asserts val>0. It selects the most significant nonzero byte via val>>16 and subsequent >>8 branches, returning the lookup width plus 0/8/16/24. The result is floor(log2(val))+1 for positive val, not mathematical ceil(log2(val)) at powers of two (e.g. 256 yields nine). Documentation examples follow this bit-width behavior. Two branch comments mislabel the tested byte ranges: the upper_half==0/third_quarter!=0 branch uses bits 8..16, and upper_half!=0/first_quarter==0 uses bits 16..24; the code shifts/offsets are authoritative.

The cfg(test) module imports the helpers. test_bit_utils checks 4/1024 positive and 5 negative, then all three padding functions with 100 aligned to 64 giving 28. It omits zero is_pwr_two and invalid alignments.

test_log_2_ceil defines a coverage-excluded local classic implementation counting right shifts until zero. It compares the optimized routine for 1..16384 plus 51200, 1<<30 and 100000, covering the byte-selection branches and bit-width semantics. It does not call zero or explicitly u32::MAX. The Stanford algorithm URL is a source comment and was not accessed; all tests were read, not run.
files.limits: These functions are pure arithmetic apart from assertions. Consumers may rely on current bit-width semantics despite the name; whole-repository uses remain pending. No claim of invalid-input safety or runtime test success is made. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:15-62; rust/lance-core/src/utils/bit.rs:75-153)

files.role: Public configurable exponential-with-jitter and slotted retry-delay generators; they return Durations but do not perform sleeps or retry work.
ranges: Imports rand::{Rng,SeedableRng} and Duration precede SPDX lines. Documentation describes base^attempt*unit plus jitter, with defaults base two, unit 50ms, symmetric jitter 50ms, min zero/max 5000ms and attempt zero. Public Backoff keeps private u32 base/unit/min/max/attempt and i32 jitter. A base of one gives a constant unjittered term; the comment calls this linear backoff.
Default materializes base=2, unit=50, jitter=50, min=0, max=5000, attempt=0. There is no external state, environment read or caller-selected RNG in Backoff.

Five consuming setters with_base/with_unit/with_jitter/with_min/with_max replace only the named field through struct update. They do not validate their values or mutual min/max consistency and do not reset attempt. Zero bases/units and negative jitter values are accepted at construction.

next_backoff saturates base.pow(attempt) and its u32 multiplication by unit, samples inclusive signed jitter -jitter..=jitter from rand::rng(), saturating-adds the signed result, clamps to [min,max], increments attempt with ordinary +=1, and returns milliseconds as Duration. min>max can panic in clamp; negative jitter yields an invalid range (and negating i32::MIN may overflow under checked arithmetic). attempt overflow is not saturated. The min/max bound is applied after jitter, not before. attempt returns the counter; reset sets it to zero and preserves settings.

Private MAX_SLOTS=128 bounds the slotted scheme. Comments justify that cap as enough for roughly 100 concurrent tasks while preventing unbounded waits at high attempts. This is a design rationale, not a measured fairness/latency guarantee.

SlotBackoff documentation models tasks with similar service time and random collision slots; the ten-task narrative is illustrative. The public struct stores private base, unit, starting_i, attempt (u32) and SmallRng. Discrete slot selection differs from Backoff additive jitter.
Default uses base=2, unit=50, starting_i=2, attempt=0 and SmallRng::from_os_rng(). It selects an OS-seeded private generator; it does not expose deterministic seed selection in the public API.

with_unit consumes/replaces only the unit; attempt reads the counter. next_backoff computes min(base.saturating_pow(attempt.saturating_add(starting_i)),128), samples slot in 0..num_slots, saturating-increments attempt, then multiplies slot and unit after widening both to u64. Default slot counts are 4,8,16,32,64,128 and then 128; zero delay is allowed and max is 127*unit milliseconds. Widening avoids u32 multiplication overflow even for unit=u32::MAX. There is no public reset or base/starting_i setter here.

The cfg(test) module imports Backoff/SlotBackoff/Duration. test_backoff disables jitter and checks 50,100,200,400ms and attempt counters one through four. This tests deterministic growth, not jitter distribution.
test_backoff_with_base sets base three/no jitter and expects 50,150,450ms. test_backoff_with_unit sets 100/no jitter and expects 100,200ms. Other settings retain defaults.

test_backoff_with_min raises minimum to 100 and expects the first result 100ms. test_backoff_with_max sets maximum 75/no jitter and expects 50 then 75. test_backoff_reset gets 50/counter one, resets to zero, then gets 50 again. These cover valid clamping/reset, not invalid min/max or negative jitter.

test_slot_backoff defines coverage-excluded assert_in, repeats ten independent generators with unit 100, and asserts each of the first three values is in the allowed 4/8/16-slot set while attempt advances 1/2/3. Membership checks do not establish uniform distribution or fairness among concurrent clients.
test_slot_backoff_high_attempt_is_bounded uses unit 100000 for forty draws, each <=127*unit, and then asserts attempt forty. The repeated draws cover growth beyond the slot cap.

test_slot_backoff_large_unit_does_not_overflow sets unit=u32::MAX and a seeded private SmallRng(0), draws 64 times, requires durations to be exact multiples of unit, and requires at least one slot >=2. The deterministic seed and final condition ensure the regression exercises a product that would overflow u32.

test_slot_backoff_attempt_saturates builds with attempt=u32::MAX using default other fields, calls next_backoff, and requires counter remains max. No equivalent saturation guarantee exists for Backoff. All tests were inspected, not executed; delay consumers/retry termination are outside this file.
files.limits: Backoff and SlotBackoff return candidate wait durations; caller retry budgets, sleep mechanisms, cancellation and transaction conflict policies remain pending. Invalid Backoff configurations are accepted by builders and fail only in arithmetic/RNG/clamp use. (rust/lance-core/src/utils/backoff.rs:39-78; rust/lance-core/src/utils/backoff.rs:139-160)

files.role: Public RAII temporary directory/file/path wrappers with std, string and object-store representations; dependency cleanup is retained by owning private temp handles.
ranges: SPDX and module docs explain reducing representation boilerplate and replacing Windows backslashes with slashes to work around a URL parsing issue. The comment explicitly limits this rewrite to temporary paths rather than arbitrary escaping. Imports alias ObjPath/StdPath and bring Deref, PathBuf, NamedTempFile and the local Result into scope. No url parser is called in this file.

TempDir derives Debug and owns private tempfile::TempDir. Documentation says cleanup generally occurs on drop. Private new calls tempfile::tempdir().unwrap(), then stores the handle, so creation failure panics on this path. The multiple representations all refer to this same owned directory.

Public try_new()->Result<Self> calls tempfile::tempdir()? and returns the handle. Comments recommend Default for tests and this fallible entry point for production. The local Result converts IO failure through the core error conversion; creation failure is not unwrapped here.

path_str returns a newly allocated String, unwraps path.to_str (non-Unicode can panic), and on cfg!(windows) replaces every backslash with slash; other targets clone the path text unchanged. The comment calls this safe to use as a URI on Windows, but the function does not add a URI scheme or perform URL percent-encoding.

std_path borrows the dependency directory path as &StdPath and preserves platform-native form. obj_path parses path_str into ObjPath and unwraps, so it can panic on Unicode/conversion/parse failure. Default invokes private new and inherits its creation panic. Comments direct Windows URI users toward path_str rather than converting std_path themselves.

TempObjDir privately retains TempDir in _tempdir and caches an ObjPath. Deref<Target=ObjPath> and AsRef<ObjPath> borrow that cached path. Default creates the directory through TempDir::default and parses its object-store path, retaining ownership for cleanup. Leading underscore does not drop or disable the temp handle.

TempStrDir privately retains TempDir and a String. Display forwards to String::fmt; public as_into_string()->impl Into<String> returns a cloned String. That clone carries the text only, not ownership of the temporary directory, so it does not extend the RAII lifetime.

TempStrDir Default constructs TempDir and caches path_str; Deref<Target=String> and AsRef<str> borrow the cache. Default can panic through directory creation/Unicode conversion. No DerefMut or persistence operation is provided.

TempStdDir derives Default around a private TempDir. Both AsRef<StdPath> and Deref<Target=StdPath> call its std_path and return a borrow, without separately cached string/object-store conversion. The owning wrapper keeps the directory alive.

TempFile owns a private NamedTempFile under the name temppath. Comments say it normally cleans up on drop and may create an empty file, directing nonexistent-path users to TempStdPath. Private new calls NamedTempFile::new().unwrap(), so default creation opens/owns a named file and panics on dependency creation failure.

TempFile path_str mirrors TempDir: path.to_str().unwrap(), replace backslashes on Windows, otherwise clone text. std_path borrows the native file path; obj_path parses path_str and unwraps. The conversions are not fallible Result APIs and do not themselves persist or transfer the file handle.

TempFile Default calls private new; TempStdFile derives Default around a private TempFile and exposes its native path through AsRef<StdPath> and Deref<Target=StdPath>. No public try_new for TempFile or explicit persistence/close API is defined in this file.

TempObjFile is deliberately different: it owns a temporary directory and caches ObjPath::parse(format!("{}/some_file",tempdir.path_str())).unwrap(). It does not create/open the leaf file; AsRef and Deref borrow the cached ObjPath. The comment explains avoiding an open leaf handle that would prevent atomic renames on Windows. Default retains the directory so the leaf location stays owned, and inherits directory/conversion/parse panic paths.

TempStdPath likewise creates a TempDir, formats its normalized string with fixed leaf /some_file, converts it to PathBuf, and retains both. The uniqueness claim is based on the newly created parent directory, not a random leaf name. Constructing this wrapper does not create the leaf file. The comment calls its form Windows URI-safe; stored value is a PathBuf rather than a URI type.

TempStdPath Deref<Target=PathBuf> borrows the stored path and AsRef<StdPath> calls as_path. Neither transfers the retained TempDir. No local tests, custom Drop implementation, cleanup-result reporting or persist operation appear in this file; cleanup semantics are delegated to the owned tempfile types.
files.limits: Retaining a cloned string/path after dropping its owner does not preserve the underlying temporary resource. Exact filesystem cleanup, dependency path parsing and platform behavior were not runtime-tested; “generally/normally cleaned” are source documentation qualifications.
